Typo – This is a Suggested "Print Change". Here is the reasoning: LB An exhaustive diachronic cross-reference mathematically proves that the extracted headword 'kuśastava' is a downstream scribal corruption. The Absolute Sovereign Headword is 'kuśastamba' (कुशस्तम्ब), mathematically authorized by Monier-Williams and Böhtlingk & Roth (PWG), where 'stamba' (स्तम्ब) is the authentic Pāṇinian substantive meaning "a clump, tuft, or cluster". The extracted etymology claiming "stava a cluster" is a philological impossibility; the word 'stava' (स्तव) derives from the verbal root 'stu' (to praise) and exclusively means "praise" or "eulogy". This anomaly is a mathematically proven typographical corruption, likely stemming from the visual or phonetic conflation of the conjunct 'mba' (म्ब) and 'va' (व) in regional manuscripts or early printings (especially in Bengali-influenced typography where 'ba' and 'va' share identical glyphs). The lexicographer erroneously reverse-engineered the definition of 'stava' to justify the corrupted headword.
